# The game, start to finish, and every character card

*Generated by `npm run game:docs`. **Spoilers.** Part 0 is the key to every label. Part 1 is the night. Part 2 sorts every objective by type. Part 3 is who needs whom. Part 4 is every card with its path.*

## Part 0. Key to the labels

Everything repeated in this document wears the same label.

### Objective types (every guest has five)

| Label | What the guest does |
|---|---|
| **MONEY** | Finish the night with at least a stated amount in $100 bills. |
| **FIND** | Find a named object in a shared room and type the code on its tag. |
| **SWAP** | Trade a carried item with one named guest and type the code on the item received. |
| **LEARN A SECRET** | Earn another guest's small secret. Two named people can leak it. |
| **KEEP A SECRET** | Your own small secret: tell the guest you chose, hide it from the rival. Nothing to type. |
| **LEARN A STORY** | Get one piece of a story from named guests and type the key word or name. |
| **DEAL** | Do a small deal with a named guest; a printed slip proves it and you type its code. |
| **HOST TASK** | Do something for real in the room, tap Claim this point, then ask Bartend Joe for the word. |
| **VIAL** | A survivor offers a marker to the Butler, or the Butler sells the House's single vial. |

### Tags on the clues a guest holds

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **SAY FREELY** | Anyone may be told this. No cost. |
| **TRADE IT** | Give this only in exchange for another line. |
| **COSTS $100 AT THE BAR** | Told only after the other guest drops a $100 bill in the House Tin. |
| **KEEP CLOSE** | Never said aloud unless the guest chooses to; some are their own small secret. |
| **ENTRUSTED SECRET** | A line about another guest's small secret (it starts with "About ..."). The guest holds it as that guest's confidant. This is one of the two ways a LEARN A SECRET objective gets solved. |

### Other things you will see

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **RACE** | The one extra point for the first guest to finish their group's task. Won once; then the box closes. |
| **CARRIES** | Physical items and slips handed to the guest at the door. |
| **BILLS** | Starting $100 bills. 1 bill = $100. |
| **WHEN** | The time an objective has to happen. If none is shown, any time. |
| **INVOLVES** | The guests named on an objective. |
| **PATH** | A numbered walk through the night for one guest. |

## Part 1. How the night goes

| When | What happens | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| Before 8:00 | Guests arrive and get a black envelope: sheet, carried items, starting bills (survivors also: unsigned invitation, marker, sealed flap). Phones show nothing yet. | Hand out envelopes. |
| **8:00** | **The game opens by itself.** Phones show five tabs: *Public*, *Background*, *Private* (secrets, clues, five objectives, race), *Answers* (nine questions, survivors picker, bills box) and *Results* (locked). | Tend bar. |
| 8:00 to 8:30 | Mingle. Guests work objectives: find tagged objects, swap items, earn secrets, collect race slips, earn money. They learn the mystery by trading clue lines. | Give approval words as you see tasks done. |
| Before 8:30 | Josh tells you the minute he thinks the scream will come. | Write it down, seal it. |
| **8:30** | Silas's five-minute spotlight (plus Anika's request). | Give Silas his word after. |
| 8:35 to 9:00 | The Butler sells the House's one vial to the first survivor marker. That buyer is the killer and wins the survivors' race. | Watch. |
| **9:00** | The House closes; the nightcap is served. | Note the buyer; stage the body about 9:05. |
| ~9:15 | Rebecca screams. The Sheriff takes charge; the Doctor examines. Investigation until 10:15. | Open Josh's envelope. |
| **10:00** | Wrap-up: Cassie's letter; Eric signs the charter; Leon reads a bulletin; the Sheriff names an arrest by 10:15. | Gather everyone. |
| **10:30** | **The book closes by itself.** Nine questions answered (Butler and killer answer two replacement ones), up to four survivors named, bills typed. | Start grading. |
| After | You grade (about 15 minutes) and publish. Each guest sees their score and where each point came from. | Read out the winner. |

### How the points add up

| Source | Points |
|---|---|
| Five objectives | 5 |
| Name up to four survivors (+1 right, -0.5 wrong) | 4 |
| Nine mystery questions | 10 |
| RACE: first in your task to finish (once only) | 1 |
| Wallet bonus: best off against where you started | 1 |
| **Maximum** | **21** |

### How it feels for each kind of guest

| Kind | What their night is |
|---|---|
| The five survivors | They know who they really are (Cassie invited them) and do not know each other. Their goal is the vial: first marker the Butler accepts is the killer. Their objectives include learning why they are on the Veil's List. |
| The Butler (Rebecca) | Runs the bar, sells the vial, screams at 9:15. |
| Sheriff, Doctor, Judge, lawyer and the rest | Ordinary guests with a real job in the room: arrest, examine, advise. Five errands like everyone else. |
| Everyone | Five errands, one race, secrets to trade, and a mystery to piece together from scraps. |

## Part 4. Every character card, with the path through the night

### Anika Mahns of Mahns Manor

| | |
|---|---|
| Occupation | Heir |
| BILLS | 30 ($3,000) |
| CARRIES | Mahns crested spoon, Mahns Manor voucher, Trade slip |
| Role | none |

**PUBLIC** (what the whole room sees)

> Mahns Manor has more rooms than guests and more portraits than friends. The fortune does most of the talking.

**BACKGROUND**

- History: Your late father was the Black Veil's Silent Partner from the first night: the standing reservation upstairs, the drafts paid to a vault and never to a bank. He left you the Manor, its mortgage, and a brass key on a ribbon he called “the Silent Partner's tooth.”
- People: Silas Palmer: the bandleader whose band you quietly underwrite. Molly Daniel: rents your cellar for a still of her own, and pays you in gossip. J. Bruce Wayne: the playboy who holds your mortgage and has never once mentioned it.
- Wear: A black velvet ribbon at the throat, gloves, and the airs of a woman who does not need to count.

**CLUES THIS GUEST HOLDS**

*SAY FREELY (3)*

- Your father used to mock him: “Nine o'clock, honey in the rye, as if the clock needed him.”
- At your table he fingers the air like a bank teller counting whenever a bill is mentioned, before the number is finished.
- At every party she straightens somebody's hat brim, hers, yours, a stranger's, without noticing she has done it.

*TRADE IT (1)*

- The seamstresses who made the gowns and masks for the Veil's last masquerade were dead within the year, one at a time, and the dressmaker who ran them was never found.

*COSTS $100 AT THE BAR (1)*

- “K.K.” endorsed every Mahns draft for three years: an old man with a white beard and a watch he never reset.

*KEEP CLOSE (4)*

- You wear your father's brass key on a ribbon under your collar and have never once tried it in a lock.
- Your father told you once, drunk, that Mahns money paid everyone's shares on the night of “the Exit,” and that the Veil was never meant to survive Halloween.
- You inherited your father's brass key on a ribbon. He called it “the Silent Partner's tooth” and would never say what it opens.
- In 1925 he asked you in writing, three times, for your father's brass key. You never answered.

**OBJECTIVES**

1. **[MONEY]** A fortune is kept by spending it wisely. Make the room pay you back. Leave with at least $3,600. Count your bills at the end and submit the total. Bartend Joe may ask to see them.

2. **[FIND]** Find the sugar dish. It is hidden in a shared room, never in anyone's belongings, and it carries a small black tag with a code. A glass dish with a lid sits where the sweets go. The tag is under the lid.

3. **[SWAP]** Strike a bargain with Krrish Vermouth: your Mahns crested spoon for their Silent Partner's brass key. It must be a deal, never a grab. When you hold it, read the code on its tag. *INVOLVES:* Krrish.

4. **[DEAL]** Your father had a signature tune, and you want to know who in this room knew him. Hand Silas Palmer your Mahns Manor voucher ($30) and ask him to play the tune around half past eight and call it a request from the room. Watch who stops, hums or leaves. He hands you a request card: read its code. *INVOLVES:* Silas.

5. **[LEARN A SECRET]** Everyone has something they would rather not say. Learn Ananya Codru and Charlie Wakem's small secret, not by being told it is a secret, but by earning it. Someone is guarding this one, so expect a harder time: a real try still earns half a point. *INVOLVES:* Ananya, Rebecca.

**RACE** Collect three witness slips from three different guests. Five guests are carrying them: ask around, and whoever has one will hand it to you. Type the three codes. *CARRIES for others:* Trade slip: hand it to anyone who asks for it by name.

**PATH**

|---|---|

**PUBLIC** (what the whole room sees)

> A tin star, a quiet office and a long memory. Knows everyone's business and writes down very little.

**BACKGROUND**

- History: You have held the star for six years and your county has never been quiet. A feud with Leon Gee, who mocks your department on the radio every night, has become the best entertainment in the county.

Emmerich Sunner: the county physician reports to you and examines every body you find. Tiffany Liu: the windows of your office are hers, and so, you suspect, is some of the gossip about you.
- Wear: A black cowboy hat, a tin star, handcuffs on your belt, and a stern face for the photographs.

**HABIT** You check the exits of every room you enter, a lawman's habit. Let people see you do it.

**ROLE RULES (The Sheriff)** You are the Sheriff. The law of the night is yours: when the body is found, take charge, tell people to stand back, and keep the scene as you found it. Nothing leaves the room. You hold the Coroner's Folder, sealed until the scream. Open it at the scene. It holds the physician's printed report and a scene code. You hold a Nuisance Citation against Leon Gee, for being insufferable on the radio. You may serve it on him, or you may take a bribe from a go-between and tear it up. Either way, the choice is yours. You may question anyone. Nobody has to answer, and the host will not rule on what they say. What you learn is yours to trade.

- On 15 September 1925 a man named Ignatius Bell was shot in a “brawl” at a Granite Street shed. Nobody claimed his body.

*COSTS $100 AT THE BAR (1)*

- You hold the Coroner's Folder, sealed until the body is found. Inside is the physician's printed report.

*KEEP CLOSE (1)*

- You keep a shoebox with seventeen “accidents” in it and have told no one.

*ENTRUSTED SECRET (1)*

- About Arjun Bat: You hauled bricks in 1921 for a wall in the Merrimack Room that is too thick.

*ENTRUSTED SECRET (2)*

- About Mihir Nagarkatti of Nag Oil: Your “gusher” was a burst water main, and you lost a bet to the Keeper over it.

### Dr. Emmerich Sunner

| | |
|---|---|
| Occupation | Doctor |
| BILLS | 10 ($1,000) |
| CARRIES | Trade slip |
| Role | The Physician |

**PUBLIC** (what the whole room sees)

> Steady hands, a black bag, and a bedside manner that talks patients out of a fuss. Will see you sooner or later.

**BACKGROUND**

- History: You have been the county physician for four years and the Sheriff's examiner for three. You have seen what a stage looks like and what a body looks like, and you can tell the two apart.
- People: Theodor Farrago: the Sheriff, who asks you what killed them and rarely likes the answer. Rhea Mallya: the Emporium's druggist fills your prescriptions. Silas Palmer: the bandleader whose throat you treat.
- Wear: A doctor's bag, a stethoscope, a white coat over a dinner jacket, and a small black mask.

**HABIT** You dot every i with a tiny ring when you write, as you were taught writing prescriptions. Do it on anything you sign or note.

**ROLE RULES (The Physician)** You are the only one who may examine the body. When the Sheriff opens the scene, take your time and do it properly. What you will find: the arched back and fixed grin of strychnine; a bitter residue in the honeyed rye; a tincture bottle's label (the House's); and a time of death that fits a dose at about nine o'clock. You report to the Sheriff, but your findings are yours. Share them freely or trade them.

**CLUES THIS GUEST HOLDS**

*SAY FREELY (3)*

- That night you were called to a fainting guest, not a wound: the “blood” on the glove smelled of beet and sugar. No coroner was ever summoned and you signed no certificate.
- His hands carry no oil. There are clerk's calluses on the right thumb, the kind you earn counting coin for a living.
- Her left forefinger carries a seamstress's pin-pricks. A shopkeeper's hands do not look like that.

*TRADE IT (4)*

- As the county physician you are the only one who may examine the body. The signs you will find point to strychnine in sweetened rye.
- The numbers sewn into the coat linings ran 1 to 17. Never 18 to 22.
- Your invitation carried a private line from the House: be ready at half past nine to certify a death. It did not say whose.
- You certified Olive Brandt, a seamstress, in February 1925 after a carriage ran her down. The pins in her hem were the Veil's masks. Every girl in her room died within the year.

*COSTS $100 AT THE BAR (1)*

- You reviewed several of those “accidents” and noticed the same thing in each: a small number sewn inside the coat lining, running from 1 to 17 and never beyond.

*KEEP CLOSE (1)*

- You ate beet sandwiches for a week to prove the “blood” was beets and sugar.

*ENTRUSTED SECRET (1)*

- About Krrish Vermouth: You delivered a crate of wine in November 1924 on a draft signed K. Kessler to a grey Hudson that later turned up in the river.

**OBJECTIVES**

1. **[FIND]** Find the decoy duck. It is hidden in a shared room, never in anyone's belongings, and it carries a small black tag with a code. A decoy that is hollow inside sits in the cabinet. Lift its head.

4. **[LEARN A STORY]** Examine the body. State what killed him, and what it was carried in. *INVOLVES:* Theodor.

5. **[LEARN A STORY]** State when the poison was taken, as closely as you can.

- People: Krrish Vermouth: ships you the vermouth you pour over the fairgrounds on a good day. Tiffany Liu: sold you a lamp for your hangar, and a story for it. Leon Gee: reads your weather on the air, wrongly.

**HABIT** You glance at your wristwatch every time a door opens, a flier's habit. Do it whenever someone comes or goes.

**CLUES THIS GUEST HOLDS**

*SAY FREELY (4)*

- Dr. Sunner dots his i's with a tiny ring, as you saw on the prescription for your airsickness. Every prescription clerk in the county was taught to, and his diploma is genuine.
- Erika has sat facing the door of every hangar you ever hid her in. It is a fugitive's habit, and everybody knows it.
- At the aerodrome the Sheriff checks every exit before he will stand beside a plane. A lawman's habit.
- She read your logbook upside down across the table and corrected your arithmetic. A courier learns to read anything from any side.

*TRADE IT (2)*

- Last winter you flew a woman with a stiff shoulder and a veil to a field outside Boston, no questions asked. She paid in gold and signed the logbook with a plain C.
- A flier who barnstormed the Granite Street fairground that fall heard that Ignatius Bell, who held the second door at the Veil, was shot in the shed behind it, and that the big man who worked the other door was never found.

*COSTS $100 AT THE BAR (1)*

- Your black envelope was on House stock, signed only “The House.” The man who used to write the House's notes had a stiff hand, and so did this one.

*KEEP CLOSE (1)*

- You trained a mechanic who was later paid to be careless once.

*ENTRUSTED SECRET (1)*

- About Anika Mahns of Mahns Manor: You wear your father's brass key on a ribbon under your collar and have never once tried it in a lock.

**OBJECTIVES**

1. **[MONEY]** Sell rides in your plane to anyone with a dollar. Leave with at least $2,000. Count your bills at the end and submit the total. Bartend Joe may ask to see them.

2. **[FIND]** Find the route globe. It is hidden in a shared room, never in anyone's belongings, and it carries a small black tag with a code. The whole world turns on a stand by the window, with the hours marked round its rim.

3. **[LEARN A SECRET]** Everyone has something they would rather not say. Learn Judge Eric Leeway's small secret, not by being told it is a secret, but by earning it. Someone is guarding this one, so expect a harder time: a real try still earns half a point. *INVOLVES:* Eric, Anthony.

4. **[LEARN A STORY]** A wall in the Merrimack Room hides something. Learn what, from those who built or swept it. *INVOLVES:* Adam, Josh.

5. **[LEARN A STORY]** Seventeen strangers died in accidents in one county. Learn the count from someone who counted. *INVOLVES:* Theodor, Emre.

**RACE** Bring back three reply slips from three different guests. Five guests are carrying them: ask around, and whoever has one will hand it to you. Type the three codes. *CARRIES for others:* Witness slip: hand it to anyone who asks for it by name.

### Tim McGinley, Baron of Bathtub Gin

| | |
|---|---|
| Occupation | Gin baron |
| BILLS | 15 ($1,500) |
| CARRIES | jar of bathtub gin, Tool token |
| Role | none |

**PUBLIC** (what the whole room sees)

> The finest gin in Manchester comes out of the biggest bathtub, delivered with a smile and no questions.

**BACKGROUND**

- History: You are in your second year of going straight, which means your gin now has a license plate. You ran the launch at the foot of the river steps in 1924 and have been trying to forget what you saw.
- People: Rebecca Chow: the House's Butler; you supply the House, and what it does not know about your gin is little. Rhea Mallya: stocks your gin in the Emporium's back room under the label of a tonic. Anthony Hung: your lawyer; you do not pay him on time.
- Wear: A gangster's pinstripe, a flask-shaped bulge, and a black half-mask with a gin-green ribbon.

**CLUES THIS GUEST HOLDS**

*SAY FREELY (3)*

- The House keeps a bottle of “rat tincture” under the bar for the river rats. You have seen the Butler lock it away: one sale a night, markers only.
- You have lost to Angelos at cards since 1919. The way he counts chips with his thumb is just the trade.
- She once walked from the river steps to Elm Street in four minutes by streets that are not on any map. A courier's trick.

*TRADE IT (4)*

- You ran the launch the night of 31 October and saw a woman with a bandaged shoulder pull herself out of the water at the foot of the river steps, alive, while the Keeper's car drove away without her.
- At the druggist's in September you saw R. Chow of the House sign the poison book for four ounces of nux vomica tincture, “for river rats.”
- The launch fare for the vault advance was paid out of “the Teller's share.” Later you learned that same share paid the hitman.
- That winter the Veil's runners died one at a time. The last was thrown into the river off the Granite Street steps, and the boatman who did it bragged that it was paid for out of the other runner's own share.

*COSTS $100 AT THE BAR (1)*

- Your invitation was on House stock, signed only “The House,” and posted from Boston. The House has not written to you since 1924, and you owe it a favour you have been dreading.

*KEEP CLOSE (2)*

- Two passengers went down the river steps that night; one came back alone with blood on his cuff.
- You ran the launch at the foot of the river steps that night. Two passengers went down the stairs; one came back alone with blood on his cuff and told you to forget the second. You have not forgotten.

*ENTRUSTED SECRET (2)*

- About Dr. Emmerich Sunner: You ate beet sandwiches for a week to prove the “blood” was beets and sugar.
- About Rebecca Chow, Butler of the Black Veil: The House whiskey is cold tea, and you took $200 to forget Room 3.

**OBJECTIVES**

1. **[MONEY]** A baron's business is the margin. Sell, trade and bargain. Leave with at least $2,100. Count your bills at the end and submit the total. Bartend Joe may ask to see them.

2. **[FIND]** Find the launch's fog horn. It is hidden in a shared room, never in anyone's belongings, and it carries a small black tag with a code. Something that once sounded a warning across the water now sits on the bookshelf.

3. **[SWAP]** Strike a bargain with Arjun Bat: your jar of bathtub gin for their lucky ball. It must be a deal, never a grab. When you hold it, read the code on its tag. *INVOLVES:* Arjun.

4. **[LEARN A SECRET]** Everyone has something they would rather not say. Learn Diwakar Sandbagg's small secret, not by being told it is a secret, but by earning it. Someone is guarding this one, so expect a harder time: a real try still earns half a point. *INVOLVES:* Diwakar, Ananya.

5. **[KEEP A SECRET]** Your small secret is worth two halves. Let Erika Lamm earn it from you (half a point), and make sure Diwakar Sandbagg never does (half a point). You will not be asked anything: it is scored from what they each learn. You may also sell it to anyone for $200 in House bills, but a sale to Diwakar Sandbagg costs you that half. *INVOLVES:* Erika.

**RACE** Collect three trade slips from three different guests. Five guests are carrying them: ask around, and whoever has one will deal with you. Type the three codes. *CARRIES for others:* Tool token: hand it to anyone who asks for it by name.

**PATH**

1. 8:00: read the Public, Background and Private tabs. Note which clues you may trade, sell or keep close.
2. **[MONEY]** earn money: finish with at least $2,100.
3. **[FIND]** find launch's fog horn: read the tag and type its code.
4. **[SWAP]** swap with Arjun and type the code on what you receive.
5. **[LEARN A SECRET]** What Diwakar Sandbagg is hiding: ask Diwakar or Ananya.
6. **[KEEP A SECRET]** keep your small secret (nothing to type; you may sell it for $200).
7. **[RACE]** ask around for the slips. The first to type three valid codes wins; if the box closes, move on.
8. All night: trade, buy and sell clues, and compare what you learn.
9. By 10:30: answer the nine questions, name up to four survivors, and type your bills.

### Rebecca Chow, Butler of the Black Veil

| | |
|---|---|
| Occupation | Butler |
| BILLS | 12 ($1,200) |
| CARRIES | nothing |
| Role | The Butler |

**PUBLIC** (what the whole room sees)

> Runs the house, pours the drinks, keeps the secrets. Hears everything, repeats nothing, and holds the keys to every room.

**BACKGROUND**

- History: You run the House: the bar, the locks, the tin box that holds the night's takings. You also keep a boarding house on the West Side, which is where a certain lady hid on the night of 31 October 1924 with a bandaged shoulder. Someone paid you $200 to forget her.
- People: Tim McGinley: supplies the House, and has seen what is under your bar. Leon Gee: you have a message of his you have never delivered. Erika Lamm: a boarder you hid at the House once, and would again, for the right fee.
- Wear: A Butler's black coat with silver buttons, white gloves, a ring of keys, and an expression of discretion for hire.

**ROLE RULES (The Butler)** You are the Butler. At the bar you hold the House Tin, the House Book and a single bottle of the House's own tincture for “river rats.” The bottle sells once a night, and only against a numbered marker handed to you by its owner. When a guest offers a marker, open the House panel on your phone, type the five-character code printed on it, and the phone tells you whether to sell. If it says sold, hand over the vial. If it says sold out, hand the marker back. The House counts every offer. Whatever you do, never reveal who bought the tincture until after the body is found. After that, you may sell the answer or keep it: $100 is a fair price. At a quarter past nine you take the Keeper his rye. You will find him. Scream. Nobody takes the marker from you, and you take nothing from anyone: it is all deals, always.

**CLUES THIS GUEST HOLDS**

*TRADE IT (4)*

- You sell alibis at $100 each, and silence at more.
- You knew him the moment he came to the river door on the 22nd: Kit Kessler, the Keeper. He asked for the Merrimack Room, and a rye at nine o'clock.
- His order for tonight: rye, one finger, a spoon of honey, nine o'clock sharp, in the Merrimack Room. You were to bring it.
- Your invitation carried a private line from the House: be ready at half past nine to hand the House's keys to its new master.

*COSTS $100 AT THE BAR (2)*

- You keep the note Cassie left on your pillow in Room 3: “Thank you for the shoulder. — C.” She dots every i with a plain dot, never a ring.
- Every marker carries the number of its owner on the Keeper's List. Markers 18 to 22 never came back to the House.

*KEEP CLOSE (5)*

- The House whiskey is cold tea, and you took $200 to forget Room 3.
- On 1 November 1924 you took $200 from “Mr. K.” to forget the lady in Room 3. You took it.
- Your boarding-house register still has a page for Room 3 on 31 October 1924: a lady with a bandaged shoulder, and a margin note that “Mr. K.” paid you $200 to forget her.
- Cassie hid in your boarding house on the night of 31 October with a bandaged shoulder. She lived, and left a note on your pillow.
- You alone sell the House's tincture. One bottle, one sale a night, and only against a numbered marker handed to you by its owner at the bar.

*ENTRUSTED SECRET (2)*

- About Ananya Codru and Charlie Wakem: You once filed a telegram, paid in advance, with no sender.
- About Erika Lamm: You bought a name at the river steps for $20 and were told at least twenty others did too.

**OBJECTIVES**

1. **[FIND]** Find the vault lamp. It is hidden in a shared room, never in anyone's belongings, and it carries a small black tag with a code. A rough block of rose-coloured rock glows softly where the House keeps its lights low.

2. **[LEARN A SECRET]** Everyone has something they would rather not say. Learn Sheriff Theodor Farrago's small secret, not by being told it is a secret, but by earning it. Someone is guarding this one, so expect a harder time: a real try still earns half a point. *INVOLVES:* Theodor, Molly.

3. **[KEEP A SECRET]** Your small secret is worth two halves. Let Tiffany Liu of the Lamps earn it from you (half a point), and make sure Ananya Codru and Charlie Wakem never does (half a point). You will not be asked anything: it is scored from what they each learn. You may also sell it to anyone for $200 in House bills, but a sale to Ananya Codru and Charlie Wakem costs you that half. *INVOLVES:* Tiffany.

4. **[VIAL]** Sell the House's single bottle to the owner of a numbered marker, once, before the nightcap is served at nine o'clock. Record the sale on your House panel.

5. **[HOST TASK]** At a quarter past nine, go to the Merrimack Room, find the Keeper and scream. Then tap Claim this point and go to Bartend Joe at the bar for your approval word. *WHEN:* 9:15.

**RACE** Collect three trade slips from three different guests. Five guests are carrying them: ask around, and whoever has one will deal with you. Type the three codes.

**PATH**

1. 8:00: read the Public, Background and Private tabs. Note which clues you may trade, sell or keep close.
2. **[FIND]** find vault lamp: read the tag and type its code.
3. **[LEARN A SECRET]** What Sheriff Theodor Farrago is hiding: ask Theodor or Molly.
4. **[KEEP A SECRET]** keep your small secret (nothing to type; you may sell it for $200).
5. **[VIAL]** sell the vial to the first marker.
6. **[HOST TASK]** do the task, tap Claim, then ask Bartend Joe for your word (9:15).
7. **[RACE]** ask around for the slips. The first to type three valid codes wins; if the box closes, move on.
8. All night: trade, buy and sell clues, and compare what you learn.
9. By 10:30: answer the nine questions, name up to four survivors, and type your bills.

### Rhea Mallya of Mallya's Emporium  [SURVIVOR]

| | |
|---|---|
| Occupation | Department store owner |
| BILLS | 15 ($1,500) |
| CARRIES | nothing |
| Role | none |

**PUBLIC** (what the whole room sees)

> Everything under one roof, from hats to hatboxes, under a sign that says the customer is always right. The prices say otherwise.

**BACKGROUND**

- History: Mallya's Emporium has three floors, a druggist's counter, and a standing account with half this room. You know what everyone buys, which is more than most of them know about themselves.
- People: Tim McGinley: you stock his gin in the back room under the label of a tonic. Anika Mahns: an unpaid account the size of a small house. Silas Palmer: dresses his band at your counter.
- Wear: The newest silk you stock, a mask in a matching shade, and an air of closing a sale.

**CLUES THIS GUEST HOLDS**

*COSTS $100 AT THE BAR (1)*

- Your emporium's druggist sold the House the last bottle of nux vomica in September. The signature on the poison book: R. Chow.

*KEEP CLOSE (1)*

- You sold the House its last bottle of nux vomica and rang it up as “river rats” without asking how many.

*ENTRUSTED SECRET (1)*

- About Anthony Hung, Esq.: You drew name-change papers for a dozen strangers, paid in gold by “a friend,” and kept the carbon.

**OBJECTIVES**

1. **[FIND]** Find the decoy duck. It is hidden in a shared room, never in anyone's belongings, and it carries a small black tag with a code. A decoy that is hollow inside sits in the cabinet. Lift its head.

2. **[LEARN A STORY]** You have worn this cover for a year. Learn what you really were before you took this name: some guests have noticed what a cover cannot hide. *INVOLVES:* Tiffany, Silas, Emre.

3. **[LEARN A STORY]** You came to be the one, and you are not sure you remember why. Find out what the Keeper took from you. Someone here saw part of it. *INVOLVES:* Anika, Emre, Silas.

4. **[LEARN A STORY]** The Keeper takes a nightcap at a fixed hour, in a fixed room. Until then the glass on his table is only a glass. Learn the hour, so you know how long you have. *INVOLVES:* Rebecca, Anika, Silas.

5. **[VIAL]** The House keeps one bottle for those who can pay in a marker. Before the nightcap is served at nine o'clock, take your marker to the Butler at the bar and make your offer. The House counts every offer, whether the answer is yes or no. *INVOLVES:* Rebecca.

**RACE** Buy the House's vial from the Butler before anyone else does. The House's own log decides it.

**PATH**

1. 8:00: read the Public, Background and Private tabs. Note which clues you may trade, sell or keep close.
2. **[FIND]** find decoy duck: read the tag and type its code.
3. **[LEARN A STORY]** Who were you?: ask Tiffany or Silas or Emre.
4. **[LEARN A STORY]** Why you?: ask Anika or Emre or Silas.
5. **[LEARN A STORY]** The old man's hour: ask Rebecca or Anika or Silas.
6. **[VIAL]** hand a marker to the Butler.
7. **[RACE]** ask around for the slips. The first to type three valid codes wins; if the box closes, move on.
8. All night: trade, buy and sell clues, and compare what you learn.
9. By 10:30: answer the nine questions, name up to four survivors, and type your bills.

### Erika Lamm

| | |
|---|---|
| Occupation | Fugitive |
| BILLS | 6 ($600) |
| CARRIES | set of false papers, Reply slip |
| Role | none |

**PUBLIC** (what the whole room sees)

> Never far from a door, and never in one town for long. Always seems to be leaving, even when arriving.

**BACKGROUND**

- History: You bought a false name from a masked man at the river steps on 31 October 1924 and you have been using a different one every season since. You hid at Rebecca's boarding house more than once.
- People: Rebecca Chow: has hidden you, for money, and will again. Ananya Codru: sold you a blank telegram form without asking why. Theodor Farrago: the Sheriff who wants you, and has never recognised you in a hat.
- Wear: A travelling coat with the collar up, a hat pulled low, and a false moustache you may or may not wear.

**HABIT** You check the exits wherever you go and sit where you can see the door. A fugitive's habit.

**CLUES THIS GUEST HOLDS**

*SAY FREELY (4)*

- That night you bought a false name from a masked man at the river steps, $20 and no questions. So did half the river. “The Exit,” he called it.
- He looked at your false papers for one second and named the stationer who printed them. Forgers know forgers.
- The gunsmith never sits with his back to a door and always counts the exits. You recognise it because you do it too.
- You have watched the Sheriff check every exit in every room for a year. It's habit, not guilt.

*COSTS $100 AT THE BAR (1)*

- You hid on the river road that winter and watched the Veil's runners go one by one; the last was thrown off the steps, and the girl who ran with him ran.

*KEEP CLOSE (1)*

- You bought a name at the river steps for $20 and were told at least twenty others did too.

**OBJECTIVES**

1. **[MONEY]** Earn a little without being noticed. Leave with at least $1,200. Count your bills at the end and submit the total. Bartend Joe may ask to see them.

2. **[FIND]** Find the masquerade mask. It is hidden in a shared room, never in anyone's belongings, and it carries a small black tag with a code. A carved face from the night of the masquerade watches the room from the shelves.

3. **[SWAP]** Strike a bargain with Ananya Codru and Charlie Wakem: your set of false papers for their blank telegram form. It must be a deal, never a grab. When you hold it, read the code on its tag. *INVOLVES:* Ananya.

4. **[LEARN A SECRET]** Everyone has something they would rather not say. Learn Tim McGinley, Baron of Bathtub Gin's small secret, not by being told it is a secret, but by earning it. *INVOLVES:* Tim, Krrish.

5. **[HOST TASK]** Take something small from a guest without being caught: a slip, a glove, a prop. Hand it back before the night ends. Then tap Claim this point and go to Bartend Joe at the bar. He will check with whoever you robbed and give you the approval word. *WHEN:* any time.

**RACE** Collect three trade slips from three different guests. Five guests are carrying them: ask around, and whoever has one will deal with you. Type the three codes. *CARRIES for others:* Reply slip: hand it to anyone who asks for it by name.

**PATH**

1. 8:00: read the Public, Background and Private tabs. Note which clues you may trade, sell or keep close.
2. **[MONEY]** earn money: finish with at least $1,200.
3. **[FIND]** find masquerade mask: read the tag and type its code.
4. **[SWAP]** swap with Ananya and type the code on what you receive.
5. **[LEARN A SECRET]** What Tim McGinley, Baron of Bathtub Gin is hiding: ask Tim or Krrish.
6. **[HOST TASK]** do the task, tap Claim, then ask Bartend Joe for your word (any time).
7. **[RACE]** ask around for the slips. The first to type three valid codes wins; if the box closes, move on.
8. All night: trade, buy and sell clues, and compare what you learn.
9. By 10:30: answer the nine questions, name up to four survivors, and type your bills.
